purpose: Structure contract that every generated Ruby fragment and .conf must satisfy. Derived from counts and structure only; installed parser source is never copied here.

provenance.method: read-only ls/grep/sed/awk/sha256sum and one read-only Python survey that wrote no files

corpus.wrapperNote: The 5 full plugins share one byte-identical 316-line wrapper after slug normalization; the platform owns it. Parser Studio emits the fragment only (decision D-1).

scope: Rules apply to artifacts Parser Studio generates (udp/tcp receivers, extensionless customized_<slug> fragment plus customized_<slug>.conf). Level MUST is enforced fail-closed in compilePair; SHOULD findings are not fatal in production but fail the variant matrix. Each rule declares its basis: corpus-invariant (MUST, matching == total in the reference corpus), corpus-practice (SHOULD, >= 95% but not all), or product-rule (MUST because the wrapper contract or the product design requires it; corpus exceptions are explained in justification). corpus.matching/total count reference artifacts that comply.

rules.referenceEvidence: 455/455 fragments contain the four markers once each, in order.

455/455 fragments end at STELLAR_PARSE_END (0 lines after). In the wrapper the next tokens are the closing ends of the inner and outer class, Plugin and Fluent; whether the platform splices only the marker region is not verified.
455/455 have no non-comment line between INIT_END and PARSE_BEGIN. 441 of 455 first lines are the INIT_BEGIN marker (indentation varies) and 10 are a date comment; 4 were not classified.
455/455 fragments contain none of register_parser, StellarInnerParseClass, module Fluent or class Parser_customized (0/455 declare them).
454/455 define initialize. Generated parsers always do, because the wrapper constructs the inner class and then calls set_inner_class_params.
rules.justification: Parser Studio always generates initialize: the wrapper constructs the inner class and calls set_inner_class_params on it. The one corpus fragment without it is not a pattern the compiler produces.

rules.referenceEvidence: 453/455 assign @parser_rule_set. The wrapper reads it through stellar_inner_class_get_parser_rule_set.
rules.justification: The wrapper reads the rule set through stellar_inner_class_get_parser_rule_set, so every generated fragment must assign @parser_rule_set; the corpus exceptions are hand-written fragments.

rules.referenceEvidence: 454/455 define parse(text); the wrapper calls @inner_class.parse(text) with a block.
rules.justification: The wrapper calls @inner_class.parse(text) with a block, so a generated fragment without parse(text) cannot work.

rules.referenceEvidence: 451/455 contain yield time, record; the wrapper forwards yielded values.
rules.justification: The wrapper forwards values yielded by parse; a generated parser that never yields produces no events.

rules.referenceEvidence: 455/455 contain parser_err_msg; the wrapper skips SaaS processing when record['parser_err_msg'] is set.
452/455 reference stellar_log_index, the key every CONF routes on.
rules.justification: Every CONF routes on stellar_log_index, so a generated fragment that never assigns it would be unroutable.

rules.referenceEvidence: 438/455 yield nil, nil for nil or empty input.
454/454 CONFs have balanced <source>/<match> sections (survey parsed all of them).
The survey recorded only <source>/<match> sections for the udp/tcp CONFs it parsed; no per-parameter uniqueness count was taken.
rules.justification: Parser Studio emits exactly <source>(<parse>) and <match>(<rule>). Anything else is a generator defect or content this contract never examined, and a repeated parameter is read differently by Fluentd (last wins) than by the checker (first wins), so it fails closed.

rules.referenceEvidence: 867/886 sources are udp (434) or tcp (433); the other 19 are other types (beats, netflowipfix, http, syslog) that Parser Studio does not generate.
rules.justification: The corpus also contains beats, netflowipfix, http and syslog sources; Parser Studio only generates udp and tcp receivers.

rules.referenceEvidence: bind 0.0.0.0 in 436/436 udp/tcp-only CONFs (886/886 sources overall). Parser Studio may still emit 127.0.0.1 when the user selects loopback (decision D-3: default 0.0.0.0, user override kept).
rules.justification: Decision D-3: the generated default is 0.0.0.0 like the reference, but an explicit loopback choice (127.0.0.1) is a supported user override, so the rule is deliberately looser than the corpus.

rules.referenceEvidence: 454/454 CONFs use exactly one distinct port across their sources.
431/436 udp/tcp-only CONFs tag every source with the file's parser name; the 5 exceptions share a parent parser's tag. Parser Studio always emits its own name.
rules.justification: Parser Studio always tags with its own parser name; the corpus exceptions reuse a parent parser tag, a pattern the compiler does not produce.

rules.referenceEvidence: 432/436 udp/tcp-only CONFs use <parse> @type equal to the parser name in every source; no source uses a different parse type.
rules.justification: Parser Studio always uses its own parser name as the parse type; corpus exceptions reuse another parser.

rules.referenceEvidence: 433/433 tcp sources include /etc/td-agent/transport_settings.conf.
424/436 udp/tcp-only CONFs have exactly one <match <name>.**> with rewrite_tag_filter; the rest share a parent tag.
rules.justification: Generated classification always uses one rewrite_tag_filter match named after the parser; the corpus exceptions route differently or not at all.

rules.referenceEvidence: 424/424 such matches set capitalize_regex_backreference yes.
stellar_log_index is the rule key in 968/975 rules overall; other keys (dstip, ids, log_type) occur only in non-Parser-Studio forwarder style CONFs.
rules.justification: Generated rules always key on stellar_log_index, the field the fragment sets; other keys in the corpus belong to hand-written rules.

rules.referenceEvidence: 420/424 have exactly one inverted rule, last, tag syslog; in 423/424 its pattern equals the last class pattern. rewrite_tag_filter 2.2.0 returns on the first matching rule, so order is semantic. Rule tags overall: session 442, syslog 445, threat 64, winlogevent 27.
rules.justification: rewrite_tag_filter returns on the first match, so class rules must precede exactly one inverted syslog guard; the corpus exceptions are not generated shapes.

rules.referenceEvidence: 431/436 udp/tcp-only CONFs carry one udp and one tcp source. Product rule: the CONF sources must equal the project's declared protocols.
rules.justification: Product rule: the CONF sources equal the protocols chosen in the project.

rules.referenceEvidence: Every class set by set_log_index (threat, session, winlogevent) has a matching route in the reference CONFs. Product rule: any class the parser can emit needs a route, or events would fall to the syslog guard.
rules.justification: Product rule: every non-syslog index the generated parser can emit needs a CONF route, otherwise those events fall through to syslog.

informational.note: message_length_limit appears in 245 of 436 udp/tcp-only CONFs (values 4096-65536, mostly 16384). Parser Studio emits the project's value. Not enforced.
Reference class patterns are unanchored (/session/, 2/436 anchored); Parser Studio emits anchored patterns, which match the same exact index names. Not enforced.
Reference CONFs start with '# <date>' and '# Modified: false|true'. Parser Studio emits a generated-artifact comment header. The platform's use of the Modified comment is not verified.

Reference @parser_rule_set is a JSON literal; 433/455 carry top_fields/vendor_fields/ns_fields. Parser Studio encodes its own camelCase JSON as base64. The wrapper reads only vendor and ignore_values, and only when running as SaaS. Compatibility with the platform SaaS utility is not verified.

Reference error records carry parser_raw_msg, timestamp, msg_class '<src>_err_msg', dev_type/dev_class. Parser Studio excludes raw text by default (decision D-4); whether the wrapper requires parser_raw_msg is tracked separately.
